result.scope_note: The 1969 Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties was adopted in Vienna on 23 May 1969 and entered into force on 27 January 1980. Article 53 codifies the principle of jus cogens, stating that a treaty is void if, at the time of its conclusion, it conflicts with a peremptory norm of general international law. The Convention was concluded in Vienna, Austria, but the location refers to the negotiation site, not the entry into force condition.
